findings.title: Blocked-email matching is case-sensitive and uses unnormalised input
findings.body: The lookup compares the submitted value verbatim with a case-sensitive string column. Signup assigns params[:email] directly to the User, so a blocked record for `bad@example.com` will not match a signup using `Bad@Example.com` (or whitespace variants), even though the domain portion of an email address is case-insensitive in normal use. This bypasses the block and splits the match statistics. Normalize and strip emails consistently when creating BlockedEmail records and before looking them up, or use an appropriate case-insensitive database comparison/index.

findings.title: Validation has a persistent side effect and double-counts signup attempts
findings.body: Calling this validator increments match_count and updates last_match_at. Validators can run more than once for one operation; specifically, UsersController#create calls `user.valid?` before the Discourse Hub check and then calls `user.save`, which runs validations again. Consequently, each blocked or do-nothing email submitted through signup is counted twice, and any caller that revalidates a record further inflates the metric. Keep validation side-effect-free and record a match once at a request/operation boundary if the counter is intended to represent attempts.

findings.title: Concurrent matches can lose match_count increments
findings.body: The counter is read into an ActiveRecord instance, incremented in Ruby, and saved later. Two simultaneous validations of the same blocked email can both read the same match_count and both save that value plus one, losing one of the matches; delayed saves can also overwrite a newer last_match_at with an older timestamp. Use an atomic database update such as `update_all` with `match_count = match_count + 1` and the timestamp, or locking, when updating these statistics.

findings.title: Rejected-email additions do not invalidate emailValidation
findings.body: The response handler adds rejected values with `rejectedEmails.pushObject`, which changes array membership. The computed-property dependency `rejectedEmails.@each` does not observe membership changes for an array of primitive strings; `@each` is for observing a named property on each item. As a result, emailValidation can remain cached as successful after the server rejects the email, and the submit button is re-enabled for the same rejected value. Depend on `rejectedEmails.[]` (or explicitly notify the property) so pushObject invalidates the validation.
